A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NS-FPN research, with readable text, equations, tables, and figures supporting a complete comparison. Both end with references; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection and segmentation experiments on IRSTD-1k and NUAA-SIRST, including component ablations, computational measurements, and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds comparator results, an SFS hyperparameter sweep, and additional feature visualizations.

M1.justification: The LFP purification procedure, spiral sampling with shared learnable offsets, cross-attention fusion, and Equations (1)–(10) remain unchanged. The expanded architecture diagram and newly documented parameter choices do not establish an algorithm revision.

E1.justification: Both versions train and evaluate infrared small-target detection and segmentation on IRSTD-1k and NUAA-SIRST. The additional analyses and visual examples remain within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds IRPruneDet, IRSAM, and SFCANet to the segmentation comparisons, while Table 4 adds HS-FPN. Figure 1 replaces the displayed SCTransNet curve with IRSAM, although SCTransNet remains in Table 5. The detection comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds an IRSTD-1k evaluation grid over attention heads H={1,2,4,8,16,32} and sampling points P={3,4,5,6}. Existing dataset splits, preprocessing, metrics, training budgets, and backbone integrations remain as reported in v1.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and the new Figure 6 test sensitivity to SFS head and sampling-point counts. The feature-purification visualization expands from one example in v1 Figure 6 to three in v2 Figure 5. Existing component and scale-layer ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, empirical error bars, or statistical significance tests. The new heatmaps report individual metric values without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds baseline scores, hyperparameter-sweep results, and qualitative examples while preserving previously tabulated scores. For example, SFCANet's new 78.46% NUAA-SIRST IoU reduces NS-FPN's reported lead over the strongest comparator from 1.66 to 0.29 percentage points; NS-FPN remains at 78.75%.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation in Equations (1)–(10) is preserved. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs, and the new hyperparameter discussion does not introduce a formal theoretical result.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a lightweight, pluggable noise-suppression FPN combining LFP and SFS to reduce false alarms and improve infrared target localization. The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain this scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations that excessive attention heads leave insufficient information per head and excessive sampling points increase computation and false alarms, supporting its H=8, P=4 selection. Existing explanations of purification and spiral sampling remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access URL in the abstract and explicitly documents the selected SFS settings H=8 and P=4, together with the channel-divisibility constraint. These are additional reproducibility disclosures, without evidence that the retained experiments changed implementation.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to IRSAM, SFCANet, HS-FPN, and anisotropic diffusion. The introduction emphasizes wavelet-based approaches, and Section 2.2 adds a contrast with HS-FPN's reliance on predefined high-frequency components, sharpening the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'NS-FPN' to 'Seeing Through the Noise,' author information is reformatted, and citations switch from author-year to numbered style. The introduction receives targeted rewriting and several explanations expand, while the overall section structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially revises the visual presentation: Figure 3 merges and redraws v1 Figures 3–4 with a detailed SFS schematic, the feature visualization expands to three examples, and new Figure 6 presents sensitivity heatmaps. Figure 1 changes its displayed comparator, and tables, captions, typography, and page layout are reformatted throughout.

improvement.justification: The added frequency-related comparators in Tables 4–5 strengthen evaluation of the central contribution, while Figure 6 supplies evidence for previously unspecified SFS settings. The expanded architecture diagram and code-access information improve clarity and reproducibility documentation. These are useful, targeted gains; the method, task coverage, and established benchmark results remain unchanged.
